reviews.evidence: Reviewed actual GitLab source (http_contract.rs, offline_http.rs, main.rs) and 5 parser + 1 binary integration test definitions. Rust --serve-readonly binds only 127.0.0.1, validates snapshot and owner-only bearer file, supports GET /health and /v1/folders without Go backend, returns non-cacheable JSON. No compiled actual HTTP request observed. Does not implement signed-in MTProto, uploads/downloads, API parity or GPUI, and user requested complete Go replacement remains unmet.

Static inspection of bounded 8192-byte headers, 3-second socket timeouts, closed connection per request, constant-time bearer comparison, token inode/permission checks, server read-only fixed loopback, no token logs, and explicit no-store/nosniff. Corrected ambiguous File::by_ref().take in 6756046e. No Cargo compiler or actual provider job traces. Production blockers: no TLS, no bounded DB row query/pagination, snapshot path reopened, sequential listener DoS potential, only parent symlink check.

findings.finding: Custom HTTP/1.1 server is only valid as Unix loopback diagnostic; no TLS/public bind, request load/backpressure, filesystem path pinning and paging; do not deploy.
Snapshot path reopened each request; huge SQLite results are materialized before response size guard. Must add pinned immutable snapshot and bounded paging before production.
